A ground furnished in parts/room-1.mjs: parlour table with four stair chairs under a hanging lantern, dresser and kitchen worktop on the west wall with flower pots, two chairs facing the hearth at x=10 z18..19, kitchen table at z21, six hanging lanterns at y=6.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with 27 blocks for this part, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; the room check reports min light 8 with 0 dark and 0 dim cells.
Walk from the front-door cell (5,3,13) reaches 72 of 73 standable cells; the room verdict is ok in that test. The real entrance is not built yet, so the walk from the true way in is unverified.
left: Real ways in are not built yet (front door (5,3..4,12) and back door (5,3..4,24) belong to the fenestration part), so `mcd room` still says UNREACHABLE from the plan's entrance [15,3,10]. Re-run once front.mjs lands.

Walk from the front-door cell reports one standable cell unreached, [4,5,22], by the worktop and flower pot on the west wall. Not diagnosed; the lane to the kitchen is clear, so it is probably the tool's cell convention, but this is unconfirmed.

The stair joiner's well column (x=9 or x=10 at z20..23) is not built yet. I kept the whole well x9..10 z20..23 empty, and the lantern at (8,6,22) sits over the well mouth without touching it. Recheck the foot and head clearance when stairs.mjs lands.

The hearth at x=10 z18..19 is the chimney part's and is not built yet. The two hearth-facing chairs (stairs facing west at x=9, z18..19) assume a campfire at the back of that firebox; the light map counted the campfire as a light source only in theory.

Palette gap: palette.json has no barrel, carpet, candle, bed, chest or lectern, so the room has no rug and no bed or storage barrels. Furniture is limited to spruce stairs, fence, slab, planks, flower pots and lanterns. Add those ids to the palette if the design needs them.
Stair facing (chairs and stairs at x=6..9) follows the toolkit rule that facing = the side of the full-height back. Not checked in a close-up render.

plan.md's checklist and elements.md have no room-specific items, so nothing was ticked. The lighting item is covered by this part only partly (the lamplighter's lanterns here; the street lamps belong to the grounds part).

waste.what: Worked out the grid by hand: converted the plan's x3..11 floor into a 7-by-11 x4..10 z13..23 text grid, then drew three layers (feet, table tops, lanterns) cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 40 cells placed by hand across three layers; two rebuild and recheck cycles to fix one dim corner.
waste.tool: A `mcd room --suggest` or a `layers` option that takes the room's floor and places lanterns at the suggested spots would have skipped the second cycle; a `mcd room --rows` output already in layers() format would have saved the hand copy.

waste.what: Chose lantern spots and checked the light by re-running make.sh and `mcd room` after each edit.
waste.cost: 3 make and check cycles, about 1 minute each.
waste.tool: `mcd room --apply-suggested` writing the lantern rows into the part file, or `mcd light` run per candidate before the build.

waste.what: Checked walking by writing a temporary rooms.json with the front-door cell as the entrance, because the real entrance is not built yet.
waste.cost: one extra temp file and one walk run.
waste.tool: `mcd walk --entrance x,y,z` flag, so the room check can take an override without a rooms file.

companions.task: Confirm the stair flight's column and rail in the x9..10 z20..23 well, so the chairs at (8,3,21) and the kitchen table keep the foot and head clear, and so the lantern at (8,6,22) sits over the open well mouth as planned.
Set the lit campfire at the back of the x=10 z18..19 firebox so the two hearth chairs at x=9 face a real fire, and so the light map counts it.
Review the six-lantern scheme (hanging at y=6 from the y=7 ceiling) with the real stairs and campfire in place, and move any lantern that clashes with a flight.
Add barrels and a rug to this room, which need palette ids the palette lacks (barrel, carpet), so the kitchen has storage and the parlour a rug.
